event_info.title: National Level Poster Competition
event_info.host_institute: R. N. G. Patel Institute of Technology
event_info.venue: R. N. G. Patel Institute of Technology, Bardoli
organizers: IEEE Signal Processing Society RNGPIT Student Branch Chapter
IEEE Women in Engineering RNGPIT Student Branch Chapter

rules: The competition is open to Undergraduate Students, Postgraduate Students, and Research Scholars from recognized institutions.
Participation is allowed in teams of 2 to 4 members.
Each participant can be a member of only one team.
The competition is open to both IEEE and non-IEEE participants.
Participants must register through the official website with complete and accurate information.
IEEE participants must provide valid IEEE ID Card proof for membership verification.
Non-IEEE participants must pay the applicable ₹50 per-person registration fee.
After registration, all submitted information and documents will be verified by the event management team.
Participants must regularly check their registration status on the official website.
The application will remain Pending until it is verified and approved.
After successful verification and approval, the participant/team will receive a confirmation email.
The confirmation email will contain the team's Unique Team ID.
The same Team ID will also be displayed on the participant's website dashboard/profile.
Participants must keep their Team ID safe for all further event activities.
Invalid information or documents may result in rejection of the registration.
After registration and verification, teams must submit their poster idea/abstract through the official website.
All submitted ideas will undergo an initial screening by the organizing/evaluation committee.
A maximum of 20 teams will be shortlisted for the final presentation round.
Shortlisting will be based on relevance to the theme, innovation and originality, technical quality, practical applicability, and clarity of the proposed work.
Only shortlisted teams will be eligible for the final poster presentation.
The decision of the screening committee regarding shortlisting will be final.

tracks: Internet of Things (IoT), Embedded Systems & Robotics
rules_and_guidelines.note: The submitted poster must have a clear connection to the selected track and the event theme.

rules: Shortlisted teams must use the official poster template provided by the organizers.
The poster must be prepared in A2 size.
The poster should present an original idea, project, research work, innovation, application, or technical solution.
The poster should be clear, technically sound, visually organized, and easy to understand.
Recommended sections include Abstract, Introduction, Proposed Approach, Results, Discussion, Conclusion, and References.
Participants must provide proper references and acknowledgements for external content, data, images, or ideas.
Participants are responsible for bringing the printed poster to the venue.
Digital presentation slides are not required unless specifically instructed by the organizing committee.
The submitted work must be original and created by the participating team.
Plagiarism, copied work, fabricated results, false claims, or unauthorized use of another person's work are strictly prohibited.
The organizing committee reserves the right to verify the originality of submitted work.
Any violation of academic integrity may result in immediate disqualification.
Only shortlisted teams will participate in the final poster presentation.
Each team will receive a total of 10 minutes for evaluation.
The presentation includes 7 minutes for poster presentation and 3 minutes for Q&A.
All team members are encouraged to participate in the presentation.
Teams must remain within the allotted time.
Participants must be present at the venue at least 30 minutes before their scheduled presentation.
The poster must be displayed at the assigned location before the presentation begins.
Participants should be prepared to explain their work and answer questions from the judges.
Judges may ask questions related to the technical content, methodology, implementation, results, and applications.
Participants must be able to explain and defend their work during the Q&A session.
The decision of the judging panel will be final and binding.
Participants must carry a valid college/institution ID card or other required identification.
Participants are responsible for their own travel and personal belongings unless otherwise communicated by the organizers.
The organizing committee will not be responsible for loss or damage to personal belongings.
Participants must maintain discipline and professional conduct throughout the event.
Misconduct, misbehavior, disruption, or violation of event guidelines may result in disqualification.
Participants must follow all instructions provided by the organizing committee and event volunteers.
The organizing committee reserves the right to make necessary changes to the event schedule or procedures. Significant changes will be communicated to registered participants.
Participants must follow all announced deadlines, instructions, and submission requirements.
Failure to follow the rules may result in cancellation or disqualification.
In case of any dispute, the decision of the organizing committee and judging panel will be final.

technical_tracks.title: Internet of Things, Embedded Systems & Robotics
